question: Vijay has ₹1224 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Ajay and Prakash and asked them to invest it at 4% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Ajay and Prakash got same amount after 18 and 19 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Vijay give to Prakash?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in their investment time = 19 − 18 = 1 year.

Ratio of their initial investments (Ajay : Prakash) = (1 + 4/100)¹ = 104/100 = 26 : 25.

Total ratio parts = 26 + 25 = 51 parts → ₹1224.

Value of 1 part = 1224 ÷ 51 = ₹24.

Prakash's share = 25 parts = 25 × 24 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount distributed = ₹1224

Rate of interest (R) = 4% compounded annually

Time for Ajay (T₁) = 18 years

Time for Prakash (T₂) = 19 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest: A = P(1 + R/100)T
